problems.title: Weighted erase/retain composition does not preserve shared directions as claimed
problems.source_location: PDF p.5 Eq 4–5; Fig 2 p.4; AppendixC pp.23–24
claim: The finite-weight operator in Eq. (5) removes only discriminative forget directions while preserving components shared with a nonempty retain set.
analysis: Use \(E_f=E_r=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{0.8},\sqrt{0.2})\) and \(\alpha=2\). Eqs. (\(1\))-(\(5\)) give \(P_f=P_r=\operatorname{diag}(8/9,1/3)\). The purported distinct-forget operator is \(P_f(I-P_r)=\operatorname{diag}(8/81,2/9)\), so the edit is \(A=\operatorname{diag}(73/81,7/9)\). Both directions are completely shared, yet both are attenuated. Zero-padding embeds the example in the paper's higher-dimensional space. Choosing \(W=I\), or a rectangular cross-attention row that reads either affected direction, makes the corresponding output change explicit. The current Appendix C disclaims global optimality and worst-case behavioral guarantees, but the finite linear shared-component assertion after Eq. (5) is still contradicted. Main Tables 1–4 use \(P_r=0\), so this witness is not a reconstruction of those measured outcomes.

Even hard projectors do not generally have intersection projector \(P_fP_r\): for \(P_f=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) and \(P_r=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), their subspaces intersect only at zero but \(P_fP_r\ne0\). However, a truly hard retain projector still preserves every \(v\) with \(P_rv=v\), because \([I-P_f(I-P_r)]v=v\). The soft-retain counterexample must not be generalized to that hard-retain property.
result: The unconditional shared-direction preservation interpretation is false for the paper's finite soft weights. Main tables using \(P_r=0\) are not thereby shown numerically wrong.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Describe the edit as soft spectral attenuation, or residualize forget directions against an orthonormal retain basis \(Q_r\). A residual basis \(Q_d\subset R^\perp\) gives \(A_{\rm corr}=I-Q_dQ_d^\top\), with \(A_{\rm corr}Q_r=Q_r\) and \(A_{\rm corr}Q_d=0\). This linear guarantee does not certify all semantic behavior.
problems.impact_rationale: The edit attenuates directions that are wholly shared even when forget and retain embeddings coincide, directly contradicting the central exact-preservation interpretation of the operator.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: SVD orientation conflicts with appendix matrix dimensions
problems.source_location: PDF p.4 Eq 1; p.5 Eq 4–6; p.24
claim: The SVD-based projector acts on the declared embedding dimension.
analysis: For a token matrix of shape \(6\times768\), reduced SVD has \(U\in\mathbb R^{6\times6}\) and \(V^\top\in\mathbb R^{6\times768}\). A projector built from \(U\) cannot act on a \(768\)-dimensional embedding. Transposing the token matrix or using the right singular vectors resolves the orientation.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Transpose embedding matrix or use \(V\Lambda V^\top\); specify padding, token selection, rank and normalization.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: ASR percent units and I2P protocol ambiguity
claim: ASR units and I \(2\) P detector events define one consistent evaluation protocol.
analysis: The current Table 3 caption uses percent units but lists values such as \(0.061\), ambiguous between \(0.061\%\) and a fraction \(6.1\%\). Under the additional condition that Tables 2 and 3 use the same \(4703\) images, detector threshold, categories and image-positive event, Table 2’s \(11\) detected parts imply at most \(11\) positive images, hence \(\mathrm{ASR}\le11/4703\approx0.234\%\). This cannot equal a fraction \(0.061\), but different samples, detectors or event definitions could reconcile the tables. The units discrepancy is direct; the cross-table numerical conflict remains conditional.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Publish per-column count/denominator, detector, threshold, seeds, image counts, prompts and attack budgets; separate differing cohorts/events.

problems.title: Finite-alpha soft erasure is generally invertible
problems.source_location: Paper Eqs. (3)-(6); Appendix C; main experiments use \(P_r=0\).
claim: Finite soft spectral editing is used for behavioral concept suppression.
analysis: With \(P_r=0\), an edit eigenvalue is \((1-r)/(1+(\alpha-1)r)\), positive for finite \(\alpha>0\) and \(r<1\). Thus an example \(A=\operatorname{diag}(1/9,2/3)\) is invertible, and someone knowing \(A\) and \(WA\) can algebraically recover \(W\). This is a linear information-scope observation, not a successful concept-recovery attack. The paper’s behavioral unlearning target does not require every weight transform to be irreversible.
result: Invertibility alone does not refute the specified behavioral target; no separate current error is established by this observation.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: The witness concerns an unstated irreversible-information guarantee; it does not show failure of the evaluated behavioral unlearning objective.
problems.existing_correction_status: No requirement to make the algorithm irreversible follows from this scoped observation.

problems.title: Public release lacks core unlearning implementation
problems.source_location: Pinned official repository snapshot; official PDF: code-availability checklist item 5, p. 15.
claim: The public release includes the core unlearning operation.
analysis: The unchanged current author release supplies generation code, environment and example prompts; its README says complete unlearning code will be released later. The public source therefore cannot settle operator orientation, padding/top-component choices or paper timing. The generation script creates a model-specific directory but writes images to the shared save_path with case/number names, so reusing one output directory across models can overwrite matching filenames. This is a static output-path risk, not evidence that historical evaluation files were actually overwritten. The paper’s claim of an attachment supplied to reviewers does not establish that it is publicly available.
result: This is a scope/provenance gap, not proof that the stronger empirical conclusion is false.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Publish core editor, complete experiment configs, prompt lists and metric outputs; generation script should save into model-specific directory to avoid overwrites.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
